geometry.description: Right circular copper-plated stainless-steel cylinder (flat end caps clamped on knife edges) with two parallel copper tuning rods of 50.8 mm diameter running the length of the cavity, ~0.5 mm clearance at each end cap. Each rod is carried by alumina armatures (top and bottom) that pivot about an axle through the end cap; the two pivots lie on one diameter, symmetric about the axis. theta = 0: arm pointing radially outward (rod at the wall); theta = 180: rod toward the centre. Pivot radius and arm length are NOT published and are INFERRED here (figure measurement + 2D frequency fit).

conditions.field_map: C uses the simulated solenoid map (CST magnet solver, 2010.00169 Fig. 4; COMSOL map, 2312.16668 Fig. 3); NOT uniform. For 2D z-uniform comparisons use uniform B and expect C_2D > C_published.

conventions.form_factor_definition: C = |int E . B0 dV|^2 / (|B_max|^2 V int |E|^2 dV) (2312.16668 Eq. 5-6), B0 = magnet map. V convention not stated (136 L vacuum vs 140 L full); report both (factor 140/136 = 1.029).
conventions.Q_definition: 2312.16668 Fig. 4c: measured LOADED Q_L (critically coupled antenna); 2010.00169: 'quality factor between 40,000 and 80,000' (type not stated)
conventions.angle_convention: theta measured at each pivot from the radially OUTWARD direction (0 = rod at the wall, 180 = rod nearest the centre) (2010.00169 Sec. II.C). In 1910.08638 Fig. 2 / 2010.06183 Fig. 16 both rods have theta = 115.5 deg counter-clockwise (as viewed) in the symmetric panel; in the anti-symmetric panel the left rod is at 129.9 deg CCW and the right rod at 129.4 deg CW (230.6 deg CCW). This matches 2010.00169 Fig. 3 ('each of the rods at 116 deg').
conventions.symmetric_vs_antisymmetric: symmetric: both rods start at the wall (theta = 0) on opposite sides and rotate in the SAME sense at the same rate -> configuration has C2 (180-deg rotation) symmetry about the axis. anti-symmetric: opposite senses -> mirror symmetry about the perpendicular bisector of the pivot line (both rods on the same side of the pivot diameter). (2010.06183 Sec. VII + Fig. 16 caption; 1910.08638 Fig. 2.) In the model frame: left rod centre = (-r_p - a cos th_L, -a sin th_L), right rod centre = (r_p + a cos th_R, s a sin th_R) with s = +1 symmetric, s = -1 anti-symmetric.
conventions.notes: frequencies in the 2D model are invariant under a global mirror, so the sense convention of a single labelled rod (e.g. 2010.00169 Fig. 5 '270 deg', measured 90.9 deg CCW = 269.1 deg CW) does not affect f.

fit.method: quadratic fit of chi2(r_p, a) on the h = 2 mm grid; 1-sigma from delta chi2 = 1

solver_class.reason: Rods are off-axis: no axisymmetric reduction. The ideal geometry (rods touching both end caps, no armatures) is z-uniform, so TM010-like f, the TM mode map of the cross-section and C with uniform B are a 2D cross-section (Helmholtz, E_z Dirichlet) problem: this reproduces the published 580/890/773/656 MHz to <= 0.5% with the inferred pivot geometry. 3D is needed for the 0.5 mm end gaps, the alumina armatures, TE/TEM and TM01p intruder modes that cause the mode crossings (Fig. 8c, Fig. 8 dips, Table I), and C with the real solenoid field map.
